description: Money returned to a payer, always reversing a specific payment (paymentId) -- never issued against "an invoice" directly, since an invoice may have been paid by more than one payment (split tender) and a refund reverses exactly one of them. Mirrors billing.payment in carrying no invoice linkage of its own; the invoice's settlements[] array is where a refund's effect on a specific invoice is recorded.

$kind.description: Optional self-identifier (cf. GraphQL __typename). Omit when the enclosing schema already names the role -- a value held under a property literally named refund is unambiguously a refund without needing $kind. Include only when this object might appear untyped outside its normal context.

amount.description: The amount returned. Non-negative -- direction is carried by the type itself (this is a refund schema), never by a negative sign; never store a negative payment.amount to represent money going back.

externalReferences.description: Links to corresponding records in foreign systems, e.g. Stripe or Shopify -- see external-reference for shape and validation. Replaces ad-hoc *Id fields scattered across schemas with one uniform array.

metadata.description: Freeform escape hatch for consumer-specific data this schema doesn't model. Deliberately non-interoperable -- a private extension zone, not part of the typed interop surface. Recommend reverse-DNS-style keys (e.g. "com.example.internalId") when multiple parties write to it.

occurredAt.description: When this refund occurred (or was recorded), RFC 3339.

paymentId.description: Opaque id of the specific billing.payment this refund reverses, keyed in the consumer's own system. Always a payment, never "the invoice" -- split tender (an invoice collected via two payments) and partial refunds both depend on knowing exactly which tender the money is coming back from, and chargeback attribution needs the same precision.

reason.description: Open-vocabulary reason for the refund, e.g. "requested_by_customer". Not a closed enum -- reason taxonomies vary by processor and business and grow faster than a schema revision cycle would keep up with.

status.description: Current state of this refund attempt. Required, unlike the absent-means-default pattern used for catalog/document statuses elsewhere in this catalog -- a money-movement record's state is a fact its producer already knows at write time, and no default here is safe: defaulting an in-flight refund to succeeded would corrupt settlement math (amountPaid, amountDue) the moment it's referenced from an invoice's settlements[].

title: Refund
